messages:
Alice: FYI saw a weird p99 'laddering' pattern during the eu->us fallback window this morning. p95 stayed ~180ms but p99 jumped 4x for ~6m. Not a pure queueing spike
Ben: can you paste a sample trace? was this on a heavy-embed workload or gen?
Alice: gen, 2k tokens typical. snippet from sampling profiler attached in thread:
```
profiler: top spans
- route_eu->us (crosszone) : 420ms
- kernel_select + warmup : 120ms
- kvcache_miss_penalty : 110ms
- microbatch_coalesce_wait : 80ms
- decode: 90ms
```
Looks like kernel_select + kv misses are the big contributors when fallback trips.
Carol: interesting — we've seen kernel selection oscillate when batch sizes vary across routes. cross-region fallbacks temporarily increase inflight variance, which can cause different kernel paths to be chosen (FP16 fastpath vs quantized matricies).
Diego: +1. In our sim yesterday, if microbatch target grows >8 while routing churns, we see kernel swap thrash and KV cache churn (hot keys pushed out). That amplifies p99.
Eve: i pulled KV hit-rate during the window:
- baseline hit: 87%
- during fallback spike: 62%
Evictions/min doubled. Cache load stayed ~same.
Frank: so there are two cascades: routing -> inflight variance -> microbatch sizing changes -> kernel selection flip -> KV miss amplification -> decode/kv penalties -> p99 laddering.
Ben: can we cap microbatching per-route during fallback? i.e. per-route max_batch=6 and aggressive flush threshold if queueing > X ms.
Alice: that's one lever. Another quick win: add a kernel-selection hysteresis window so we don't flip kernels for a single batch size outlier. small change but could prevent thrash.
perf-bot: perf/trace uploaded: https://internal.perf/reports/2045007777/trace.tar.gz : contains sampled kernel traces + kv eviction timeline
Carol: also consider making KV cache replicas regional-aware on fallback: prefer local read-throughs first and backfill slowly when traffic returns. That reduces immediate miss storm.
Diego: i ran a controlled replay in staging with two options:
1) hard microbatch cap 6 -> p99 reduced 45% but throughput -8%
2) kernel hysteresis 200ms window -> p99 reduced 35%, throughput unchanged
Logs:
```
staging-replay-1: p95 170ms p99 310ms rps -8%
staging-replay-2: p95 172ms p99 360ms rps ~0%
```
Frank: given SLOs, i'd prefer combination: hysteresis + per-route cap during fallback windows. retains throughput while limiting tails. Also add a short KV prefetch for hot prefixes during expected failovers.
Eve: opened issue with metrics I used: https://redwood/ops/issues/IRIS-4022 — includes hit-rate heatmap by region and a diff of eviction sets.
Ben: action items: 1) Alice will enable kernel hysteresis flag in canary (today) 2) Diego will run broader replay with per-route microbatch caps (tomorrow) 3) Carol to prototype regional kv-read preference (next week) 4) Frank to add dashboard for 'p99 ladder index' (queue variance + kernel switches)
Alice: I'll flip the flag to canary at 11:30 PT and watch p99. ping me if you see regressions. :eyes:
Frank: if canary looks clean we can roll to prod with per-route cap as opt-in for 48h.
Diego: note — we should also add a small metric for 'kernel_switch_rate' exposed per node so we can correlate. cheap to add to agent.
perf-bot: canary started: deployment id dpl-2045007799 at 2045007900
Alice: thanks all. i'll post short summary after the 1h observation window.
Ben: TY — nice triage flow. :thumbsup:
